about.title: Home words: water, home, TV
about.length_note: About 8 minutes. Three new words, a few matching games and a short review of yes, no and help fit comfortably. You can pause after any word and come back later.

say.text: Hello {name}. Today we learn three words you see at home: water, home and TV. Go at your own speed. You can stop and look for as long as you like.
First, a quick look back. Last class we read three important words. Read them with me: yes. no. help.
Our first new word is water. Picture a clear glass of water on a table. Look at the word. It begins with a W, and it ends with an R. Say it with me: water.

show.text: A tall clear glass of water on a kitchen table. Beside it, the word 'water' in large letters.

say.text: Let's see if you can pick it out. Take your time.

ask.why: Water starts with W and ends with R. It is the only word here that begins with W.

say.text: Next is home. Picture a house with a door and a window. The word starts with H and has an E on the end. Say it: home.

show.text: A small house with a front door and one window. Beside it, the word 'home' in large letters.

say.text: Here is a tip. In home, the last letter, E, is silent. We see it but we do not say it. You say home, not home-eh.

ask.why: Home starts with H and ends with a silent E. Help also starts with H, but it ends with P.

say.text: Our third word looks different. TV is two capital letters: a T and a V. They stand for a longer word, television. We say the names of the letters: tee, vee. TV.
So with TV, we do not sound it out. We know the letters T and V, and together they mean the TV in the room. Try it.

show.text: A television on a stand. Beside it, the two capital letters 'TV'.

ask.why: TV is the only choice made of two capital letters, a T and a V.

say.text: Now we match words to pictures. Look at the picture on the left. Find the word on the right that goes with it.

show.text:
Left: a house, a glass of water, a television.
Right: water, TV, home.

say.text: First picture: a house, with a door and a window. Which word goes with it?

show.text: A house with a door and one window.

ask.q: Which word goes with the picture of the house?
ask.why: A house is where we live, and the word for it is home.

say.text: Second picture: a glass of water on a table. Which word goes with it?

show.text: A glass of water on a table.

ask.q: Which word goes with the picture of the glass?
ask.why: The glass holds water. The word water starts with W.

say.text: Now a mixed review, with our old words too. Someone asks, 'Would you like some water?' You would like some. Which word do you choose?

show.text:
yes
no
help
water
home
TV

ask.q: Someone asks, 'Would you like some water?' You would. Which word says that?
ask.why: Yes means you agree. No would mean you do not want any.

say.text: One more. You need someone to come and be with you. Which word is the important one?

ask.q: You need someone to come and be with you. Which word do you point to?
ask.why: Help is the word for asking someone to come and assist you. It is one of our three important words.

say.text: Well done, {name}. Today you met water, home and TV, and you picked each one out. Next time we learn the sounds of letters and how to join them together.

show.text:
water
home
TV
(and yes, no, help)

notes.topic: Capital letters that stand for a word (TV)
Silent E at the end of a word (home)
